title: Slack Integrations - 2022-01-26 - Workshop
content:
Our topics for this innovation day (examples):

  • Concur on what (technical) method we should use and recommend for Slack ↔︎ GitHub integrations

    • Caveats, future proof, deprecation, etc

    • Gather the information so that we can document the approach later

    • Start with a manual click approach - investigate if the solution can be automated

    • Confusing entry points: https://slack.github.com/ vs https://api.slack.com/apps

      • We’ll document this - users/teams must know the entry point/landing page

  • Experimental

    • Create new temporary channel in slack to test

    • Investigate and discuss pros & cons - limitations - what information can we get, what’s missing?

    • Exercise: Publish DORA metrics (own) changelog to slack channel

      • First to temporary channel

      • Then to target channel(s) (#ipex-devops-team, ipex-devops)?

  • Slack bot: Create issues (to our board) to Jira

    • Test, evaluate

    • Can these requests be put in some kind of “pending” state, so that we may have the chance to answer the question(s) before an actual item is created?

  • Slack workflows 

”

A bot is a type of Slack App designed to interact with users via conversation. A bot is the same as a regular app: it can access the same range of APIs and do all of the magical things that a Slack App can do. But when you build a bot for your Slack App, you're giving that app a face, a name, and a personality, and encouraging users to talk to it.

“

Findings

We divided the topic area into a couple of separate tracks:

  • Workflows

    • How to automate e.g. user onboarding messages, notifications, and collaboration

      • Outcome: This is an easy task that adds value

    • Promising opportunities to Create and track a new bug with Integration+ for Jira | Slack Tips | Slack

      • Investigate further: support using forms/templates

  • API Integrations

    • How do we deal with deprecation of webhooks?

    • How are IPEX teams currently using GitHub ↔︎ Slack integrations?

      • Nearly all teams currently use webhooks

    • What is the status of global GitHub gists in relation to Slack integrations?

      • To be investigated further, but many examples with webhooks

Workflows

  • Getting started

    • Add name and trigger

    • Add the steps (standard, custom, …) including variables

    • Add collaborators

      • Note: Only administrators can create new flows

        • Investigate: can collaborators also do that via delegation of e.g. permissions?

    • Publish the workflow - create test channel if needed

API Integrations

One of the goals was to investigate the deprecation of webhooks, and what other alternatives exist. We’d not like to recommend outdates approaches, even if they are widespreadly used within the organization, and/or within the GitHub community as such.

  • Slack App Integration

We investigated how default webhooks can be replaced via default Slack Web API invocations, via the Slack app: The conclusion is that it is fairly complex to set it up:

  • App needs to be created

    • Different landing areas in terms of which token should be used

    • App needs to be configured appropriately

    • App needs to be explicitly integrated in the Slack app

    • Scopes need be to be assigned and configured

    • Issues with invocation of the API endpoint

      • Currently, as of this writing, open case in GitHub

Conclusions

  • There are plenty of implementations using webhooks for GitHub ↔︎ Slack integrations

    • These are simple, less complex to configure, and will most likely stay for a while

  • Web API via App currently yields:

    • {"ok":false,"error":"missing_scope","needed":"chat:write:bot","provided":"incoming-webhook"}

    • This is, as stated, currently an open case

    • This may be an alternate approach to followed up - but induction of complexity is our main concern right now

  • As of now, we’ll recommend using "Technique 3"

Other Outcomes

While the majority of time was spent on the actual topic, we had the time to discuss, and conclude, the following items as well:

  • GitHub Security

    • Exposure of secrets

      • Items found

    • Initiate a Generic Requirements to initiate the work

    • Conclusions regarding how to address the concerns to the different teams/repositories involved
